title: Finite limits after restricting a flat sheaf to a slice
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, let $U$ be an object, and let $\mathcal F$ be flat. Then the tensor functor $\mathcal G \mapsto \mathcal G \otimes_{\mathcal O_U} \mathcal F|_U$ preserves finite limits on the slice site.

proof.text: Let L be sheafified direct-sum extension, T tensoring with F, and TU tensoring with F restricted to U. Extension preserves zero morphisms: its direct-sum maps send every summand to zero, and sheafification preserves zero. Rewrite the extension exactness equivalence as S.Exact iff (S.map L).Exact for every short complex S on the slice.

Evaluate the natural extension tensor comparison at each pair (G,F), and compose with tensorObjIsoSheafification on the slice and its inverse on the original site, obtaining TU composed with L naturally isomorphic to L composed with T. Naturality is the composite of the two tensor/sheafification naturality squares and the projection formula square at (f,id F).

Flatness supplies finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation by T. Extend an exact short complex S using the equivalence of step 1, then apply T. Transport this exactness through the short-complex isomorphism induced by step 2, and reflect it back using step 1. Thus TU preserves exactness of every short complex. Tensoring is additive, so Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_map_exact and Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesHomology give finite-limit preservation.
